name: Question 2
problem:
According to the flux form of Green's theorem, the flux of the vector field 
$F(x,y)=⟨y+2{x}^{2}y,\,{x}^{2}-x{y}^{2}⟩$
across the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(2,1),$ and  $(0,1)$ can be represented as

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $C$ is traversed counterclockwise, $n$ is the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C,$ and $D$ is the region bounded by $C.$ Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/98d7da0c7cd1e1f1006c1db74ae1a1e1f198d9066df6585745ee36548f0b8d96.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=y+2{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}-x{y}^{2}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=4xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the flux form of Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4xy+(-2xy))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2xy\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=2xy.$

∮CF⋅nds=∬Df(x,y)dA,

where C is traversed counterclockwise, n is the outward-pointing unit normal vector to C, and D is the region bounded by C. Calculate the function f(x,y).

EXPLANATION

Let C be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let D be the region bounded by C. If F=Pi+Qj, and P and Q have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing D, then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

∮CF⋅nds=∬DdivFdA,

which is equivalent to ∮CPdy−Qdx=∬D(∂P∂x+∂Q∂y)dA.

The region D and the curve C for this case are shown below.

We have that P(x,y)=y+2x2y and Q(x,y)=x2−xy2. So,

∂P∂x=4xy,∂Q∂y=−2xy.

Therefore, applying the flux form of Green's theorem, we get

∮CPdy−Qdx=∬D(∂P∂x+∂Q∂y)dA=∬D(4xy+(−2xy))dA=∬D2xydA.

Hence, f(x,y)=2xy.
